title: Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rav Chisda’s student, sitting before him in [Zevachim 115b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.115b.6). Hyman reports that Shitah Mekubbetzet and the Bach read Rav Chuna. In [Nedarim 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.65b.3) he objects to Rabbah; Hyman reports that Piskei HaRosh reads Rav Chana. In [Gittin 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.43b.5), Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina speaks in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name (Hyman gives Rav Chanina son of Rabbi Ketina for [Gittin 38a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.38a.18)). In [Chullin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.17b.13), Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina speaks in Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name; Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Chana. Hyman considers it very likely that he is Rav Chana bar Rav Ketina; see that entry.[^3]

notes.text: Chuna, Chana, Huna and Chanina are meaningful reported variants. The identification with Rav Chana bar Rav Ketina remains Hyman’s conjecture.

The consulted Zevachim 115b names Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina sitting before Rav Chisda. Hyman reports Chuna, Chana and Chanina variants in other editions and proposes the identification with Rav Chana; those exact Shitah Mekubbetzet, Bach, Piskei HaRosh and Dikdukei Soferim readings were not independently inspected.

The two Gittin passages transmit a case in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name. The consulted 43b names Rav Huna bar Ketina; 38a has Rav Chanina bar Rav Ketina. Nedarim directs the question to the rabbis collectively. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=960&lang=en) gathers the parallels. The other edition spellings and proposed identification remain Hyman’s.
